definitions.explanation: To cause something to happen as a consequence, especially something undesirable such as a disease, accident, or reaction.

examples.japanese: ストレスが{病気|びょうき}を{誘発|ゆうはつ}する。
{大雨|おおあめ}が{土砂崩|どしゃくず}れを{誘発|ゆうはつ}した。
この{薬|くすり}はアレルギー{反応|はんのう}を{誘発|ゆうはつ}する{可能性|かのうせい}があるので、{注意|ちゅうい}が{必要|ひつよう}です。
examples.english: This medicine may trigger an allergic reaction, so caution is needed.

notes:
{誘発|ゆうはつ} means to induce or trigger something, typically something undesirable such as a disease, disaster, or negative reaction. It implies an indirect causal relationship.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {病気|びょうき}を{誘発|ゆうはつ}する (trigger an illness)
- {事故|じこ}を{誘発|ゆうはつ}する (cause an accident)
- アレルギーを{誘発|ゆうはつ}する (trigger an allergy)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {誘発|ゆうはつ} vs {引|ひ}き{起|お}こす: {誘発|ゆうはつ} is more formal and implies an indirect cause, while {引|ひ}き{起|お}こす is more general and can describe direct causation.
